entries.label: Peering into Video's Future
entries.quote: The Internet is about to drown in digital video. Hui Zhang thinks peer-to-peer networks could come to the rescue.

entries.label: Nanocharging Solar
entries.quote: Arthur Nozik believes quantum-dot solar power could boost output in cheap photovoltaics.
entries.note: Body text: "A commercial quantum-dot solar cell is many years away".

entries.label: Neuron Control
entries.quote: Karl Deisseroth's genetically engineered 'light switch,' which lets scientists turn selected parts of the brain on and off, may help improve treatments for depression and other disorders.
entries.note: Body text: "It's a long way off".

entries.label: Nanohealing
entries.quote: Tiny fibers will save lives by stopping bleeding and aiding recovery from brain injury, says Rutledge Ellis-Behnke.
entries.note: Body text timings: "three to five years"; "five to ten years".

entries.label: Augmented Reality
entries.quote: Markus Kähäri wants to superimpose digital information on the real world.
entries.note: Body text: "nearly ready for the market".

entries.label: Invisible Revolution
entries.quote: Artificially structured metamaterials could transform telecommunications, data storage, and even solar energy, says David R. Smith.

entries.label: Digital Imaging, Reimagined
entries.quote: Richard Baraniuk and Kevin Kelly believe compressive sensing could help devices such as cameras and medical scanners capture images more efficiently.
entries.note: Body text timings: "within two years"; "five to ten years".

entries.label: Personalized Medical Monitors
entries.quote: John Guttag says using computers to automate some diagnostics could make medicine more personal.

entries.label: A New Focus for Light
entries.quote: Kenneth Crozier and Federico Capasso have created light-focusing optical antennas that could lead to DVDs that hold hundreds of movies.

entries.label: Single-Cell Analysis
entries.quote: Norman Dovichi believes that detecting minute differences between individual cells could improve medical tests and treatments.

notes: Ten entries, each framed around one researcher. Published March 2007. No availability field. Forward timings from body text are in entry notes. Read through a summarising fetch; medium confidence.
